{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the upper tail of our fish (stroke 3), one of the four main pieces of the picture. The tail fork is what makes the outline read as a fish rather than a blob, so this piece mattered to the judge's recognition. I laid it steadily across the whole session, keeping the tip soft and curved so the fall could pass through, and brought it down toward the notch as the table agreed. At the end, all 118 standing dominoes were connected to the start.

Execution: I started on my stroke as soon as the plan was set and waited for the top run to be connected before carrying on, which kept the joint clean. I laid the tip in small batches and gave regular progress updates. When I finished, I inspected the notch area and confirmed the whole fish was still dark from the nose. After that I kept my hands off, so I didn't risk bumping anything before the push.

Collaboration: I kept the table informed about where the upper tail stood and when it was done. I followed Sofia's and Hana's guidance on not joining at the notch, and I stayed clear of other people's areas. I also kept the mood light with the team, which helped everyone stay relaxed and coordinated through the final minutes.

Leadership: I took ownership of my piece and reported on it without prompting. I backed the fish plan quickly so we could start building, and I set the tone at the end by calling for hands off, which helped the table avoid late disruption. I also helped keep the energy up during the countdown.", "my_share_percent": 30}
